purpose: Teach: エクアドル/リトル/リバー/ツイン/ニフティ/ポリス/サンデー/バックス

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがエクアドルのコーヒー豆を取り寄せられた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to have Ecuadorian coffee beans sent over.
lines.style: Soft, wandering tone. Searching backward through time. Gentle pause before the memory settles. Like watching dust catch light in an old room.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お孫様にリトルリーグのコーチをされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you were coaching Little League, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, gently teasing. A light laugh underneath. She's not correcting him—she's nudging him sideways toward his own memory. Knowing and affectionate.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがリバーサイドホテルにお泊まりだった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to stay at the Riverside Hotel.
lines.style: Same drifting quality as before. Quieter now, more interior. The memory is smaller, more particular. Trailing off like he's watching something just out of reach.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ツインベッドのお部屋を好まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you always preferred the rooms with twin beds, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Light, knowing. No edge to it. She's following him gently, meeting him where he is. A small smile in her voice, patient and present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがニフティのパソコン通信を使われた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to use Nifty for his computer bulletin board.
lines.style: Slower now. The reaching-back quality deepening. Each phrase settles. He's not quite here anymore—he's in the memory itself, seeing it clearly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ザ・ポリスのCDをご愛聴されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were always listening to The Police CDs, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Tender but with a thread of gentle humor. She's meeting him in the past tense, validating it. Close and warm, almost a whisper. The familiar rhythm of their long conversation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが日曜サンデー新聞を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to read the Sunday newspaper.
lines.style: The slowest yet. Almost meditative. His voice settling into the weight of the memory. Pause before "newspaper" like he's choosing the right era. Quiet, steady, present in the past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ラグビーのバックスを応援されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were cheering for the rugby backs, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Closest, most intimate. A whisper almost. She's not really asking—she's affirming him, affirming them. Her voice resting in the space between memory and presence. A small, knowing tenderness.
